//: Spoken names are DATA, not logic. Nothing in the runtime or the skills knows that 'kimi' or 'sol' means anything: `resolve` matches a phrase against these lists. Adding a model, a backend, or another way of saying one, is an edit to this file and nothing else. Speed words (fast, quick, cheap, standard, full) are handled by resolve and are not listed here, so 'fast kimi' needs no entry of its own.
//backends: Two ways to actually run a model. `opencode` drives a local OpenCode server, which is how the non-OpenAI models are reachable. `codex` shells out to the Codex CLI, which runs OpenAI models on the ChatGPT sign-in rather than through a paid API key. Each alias names the backend it should use by default, and saying a backend word out loud overrides it: 'opencode sol' forces the OpenCode path. A backend also carries runsOn: which execution path it uses, which is not always itself. openrouter runsOn opencode, because OpenRouter is a provider reached through the same local server rather than a second way of running a job. Saying "openrouter" therefore swaps the provider and changes nothing else: same server, same agent config, same permission policy. Without this an alias could only have one provider per backend, and picking the other one meant editing the user's config by hand.

codex.description: The Codex CLI (codex exec) on your ChatGPT sign-in.

openrouter.description: OpenRouter, reached through the same local OpenCode server.

kimi.description: Moonshot Kimi K3.1 Pro. General purpose primary worker. Runs on OpenCode Zen; say openrouter to run it there instead. No fast tier yet: "fast kimi" runs K3.1 Pro at standard speed and says so.
kimi.//: Plain "kimi" follows the newest Kimi, now K3.1 Pro. Routed to Zen before Zen listed it (2026-10-28), so until it does, a plain "kimi" refuses with route_unavailable and "openrouter kimi" runs it now. Fireworks does not list it. The previous model stays reachable by its own name as kimi-k3, which keeps the Fireworks fast route.

kimi-k3.description: Moonshot Kimi K3, the Kimi before K3.1 Pro. Say "kimi k3". Has a fast tier on Fireworks.
kimi-k3.//: Kept when kimi moved to K3.1 Pro, so the older model is still reachable by name. Matching is by whole word, so "k3" never matches inside "k3.1".

glm.description: GLM 5.3 Flash. The only routed GLM: cheap, quick, good for narrow mechanical work.
glm.//: Both tiers point at the same model on purpose. GLM has exactly one routed model, so 'glm' and 'fast glm' are the same request and there is no substitution worth reporting. 5.2 and plain 5.3 are retired above, not merely absent.

sol.description: GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol). Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in unless you say opencode.
sol.//: Plain "sol" follows the newest Sol, now gpt-6.1-sol. The previous one stays reachable by its own name as sol-6, so saying "gpt 6 sol" still gets exactly gpt-6-sol rather than a newer model. When 6.1 was added, OpenCode listed opencode/gpt-6.1-sol and Codex on a ChatGPT sign-in answered it with a 400, so a plain "sol" job fails within seconds there until OpenAI enables it; "opencode sol" runs it now. Routed explicitly because Codex's model cache is not evidence either way.

sol-6.description: GPT-6 Sol (gpt-6-sol), the Sol before 6.1. Say "gpt 6 sol". Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in unless you say opencode.
sol-6.//: Kept when sol moved to gpt-6.1-sol, so the older model is still reachable by name. Its spoken forms are all longer than "sol", so they win the longest-match and never fall through to 6.1.

luna.description: GPT-6 Luna (gpt-6-luna). Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in unless you say opencode.
luna.//: Replaced gpt-5.6-luna. The 5.6 names are retired above rather than pointed here, because saying "gpt 5.6 luna" and getting a different model is the substitution this table exists to prevent. Routed explicitly rather than as pending ids, because Codex's model cache is wrong in both directions: it listed gpt-6-luna while Codex answered a ChatGPT-account request for it with a 400, and it dropped gpt-6-astra while astra ran fine. Until Codex serves it on this account, a codex job fails within seconds with that 400, and "opencode luna" runs it on the API key.

astra.description: GPT-6 Astra, the GPT-6 model that is live today. Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in; say opencode to run it on the API key instead.
astra.//backend: Live on both backends and routed explicitly, not as pending ids. As pending ids it depended on Codex's models_cache.json listing gpt-6-astra, and Codex rewrites that file in place: a resolve that landed mid-rewrite read no Codex inventory, never promoted the Codex route, and refused astra on its default backend. An explicit route follows the Codex rule in codex.mjs instead, where an unreadable cache means unverified rather than absent. Codex is the default because it bills the ChatGPT sign-in rather than a metered key. Bare "gpt 6" no longer means astra: GPT-6 is three models now, and that phrase is retired above so it asks which one.

terra.description: GPT-6.1 Terra (gpt-6.1-terra). Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in; say openrouter to run it there instead.
terra.//: OpenCode Zen does not list gpt-6.1-terra, so the second backend is OpenRouter rather than opencode. The 5.6 Terra names are retired above so they refuse instead of matching "terra" and quietly running 6.1.
